chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Trying to record songs from the show
summary: Many viewers wanted a record; she sang 'Thank the Good Lord I'm Not Old' and a label agreed to record two songs.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You also said something off tape about some of the circumstances around your efforts to have a record made of the songs you sang?

Yeah, well not strangely enough, alot of people who caught the show asked when are you going to make a recording of "A Little Stardust Left". But the clause in these equity contracts states that if there's a recording made it has to be a cast album, which means that they would have to have all the music on an album with the cast members. So there was no way that they could issue, you know, the one side of it. But before, when we were doing rehearsal I taped for the producers and for the directors two selections, "There's A Little Stardust Left" and one of the other songs in the

show, "Thank The Good Lord I'm Not Old". And I was just saying, in fact while the show was running I said, Gee, you should have copies of this in the lobby. You could either sell them or give them away." This would have been promotion for the production but they never got around to doing that. And recently the young man who is affiliated with the American Theatre, Bill Riley, who is the coordinator for talent. After you have been in a Broadway production or you get into Equity, affiliated with Equity, you usually volunteer to do performances at hospitals or whatever, you know. So Bill Riley is the coordinator for this activity and he was very enthusiastic about trying to do a recording of "Starch" and I told him to get in touch with Mel. And of course Mel and Norman were agreeable, but it seems that whoever he was talking to thought that it didn't have enough commercial value which is one of the facets of the business. But now-a-days I think that if they put out a little 45 it would do very well. It's all speculation. I mean, they could do it themselves. I wouldn't want to get involved with doing it myself but I mean if he could come up with somebody whose interested, I mean, I'd be

very willing to record the two songs. And then, as I said before, they got the tape and they could just press that. I don't know just exactly what the possibilities are about reviving "My Old Friends" because even moving from one theatre to the other like we did, you lose a certain amount of momentum. And when you open up in a new theatre you got to start all over again. It's been over a year now since it closed and it would really be like starting all over again. And at these prices you have to raise alot of money to get a show. And too, the cast members are scattered about. And who know, I'm waiting for it to come out in published form and maybe we'll get a vocal amateur group to do "My Old Friends" with the permission of the authors of course. I still think it was a very charming play and if we had stayed at the Orpheum perhaps, it might still be running. We were at the Orpheum during the worst part of the year. We were there during all the cold weather. And of course the Orpheum's a little bit out of the way. That's off-Broadway, 2nd Avenue, a little hard to reach. We drew pretty good crowds; but if we'd stayed there a little longer I think we would have - I think we should have stayed there,
